nodes.title: Even power sums in terms of $\binom{2n+m+1}{2m+1}$

Then $2^{2k-1} S_{2k-1}(n) = \sum_{m=1}^{k} Q_{k,m}(n) \binom{n+m}{2m-1}$.

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ be a natural number, let $(a_m)_{m \ge 0}$ be a sequence of real numbers, and write $S_j(n) = 1^j + 2^j + \dots + n^j$. Then $\frac{S_{2k}(n)}{2n+1} = \sum_{m=1}^{k} a_m \binom{n+m}{2m}$ for every natural number $n$ if and only if $S_{2k-1}(n) = \sum_{m=1}^{k} \frac{2m+1}{m}\, a_m \binom{n+m}{2m}$ for every natural number $n$.
